projects.name: unoq-braccio
projects.title: Arduino UNOQ Braccio
projects.description: Braccio Robotic Arm for pick and Place
projects.readme:
Control a TinkerKit Braccio arm with an Arduino UNO Q, ROS 2, Edge Impulse, and Gazebo.

Architecture details: docs/architecture.md.
highlights: ROS 2 USB serial and remote TCP bridges that convert
A Gazebo/ros2control simulation with a gripper camera, an overhead camera,
Edge Impulse integration for camera object detection and classifier-driven
USB camera vision with OpenCV color tracking.
A browser dashboard and App Lab apps for remote control.

sections.title: Edge Impulse Integration
sections.blurb: Use Edge Impulse to turn classifier labels into Braccio poses.

sections.title: Cube detector test (Edge Impulse TFLite)
sections.blurb: Runs the Edge Impulse cube model on still images or a live webcam and shows the detections on screen. It is a stand-alone check of the model; it does not use ROS.

sections.title: Braccio Web Control
sections.blurb: Browser dashboard for controlling the UNO Q Braccio over the network.

sections.title: Braccio Remote Agent for Arduino App Lab
sections.blurb: Run this app on the UNO Q when you want ROS 2 on another computer to control the Braccio over the network instead of over USB serial.

sections.title: Braccio Smoke Test for Arduino App Lab
sections.blurb: This is a minimal Arduino App Lab project for validating that the Braccio shield is seated on the UNO Q and that the MCU can drive the servos.

sections.title: Braccio Web Agent
sections.blurb: Run this single App Lab app on the UNO Q for the web dashboard.

sections.title: UNO Q USB Camera Streamer
sections.blurb: Run this App Lab app on the UNO Q when a USB camera is plugged into the UNO Q and ROS 2 is running on another computer.

sections.title: UNOQ Braccio Bridge Brick
sections.blurb: Reusable App Lab brick for controlling a TinkerKit Braccio shield from an Arduino UNO Q.

highlights: 📷 100% Passive & Camera-Free: Zero optical cameras or audio microphones. Respects user privacy while maintaining spatial awareness.
🧱 Wall-Penetrating Motion Detection: Uses 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi CSI signal distortion to sense movement behind solid walls.
⚡ Battery & Solar Powered: Low-power architecture with TP4056 Type-C charging and an 80x40mm 5V solar panel.
🐱 Cyberpunk Cat Enclosure: Compact, cute, 3D-printable cat-themed handheld chassis designed in Autodesk Fusion 360.
Distance Estimation: Calculates physical attacker proximity using Received Signal Strength Indicator (RSSI).
